justification: Standard: wakes two development-process hooks that never ran (they read TOOL_INPUT, which Claude Code does not set), deletes a third that duplicated .githooks/pre-commit, and adds a test that every registered hook reacts to its payload on stdin. No database, no served output, no customer-facing text. Not Minor: once live, the two hooks can block commits and pushes.

pre_impl.existing_data: None. Inputs are the hook payload (JSON on stdin), git state of the working tree, and .claude/.push-attempts.json.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The three hooks assumed Claude Code sets TOOL_INPUT. It sends JSON on stdin instead, so each saw an empty command and exited 0. .claude/.push-attempts.json existed nowhere, which push-retry writes on every push.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Replay of the last 30 recorded commit/push commands, each against the repo state when it ran: the two woken hooks block 0. The third, once woken, blocked 5 wrongly (3 first commits with no report yet, 2 qa_gate time-outs at 30 s); .githooks/pre-commit lines 262-280 already does its job and lets first commits through, so it was deleted rather than patched.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: The operator is the user: a wrongly blocked commit or push. Measured 0 of 30.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Either woken hook reverted to its origin/main version (reads TOOL_INPUT only), or a hook is added to settings.json with no must-react case and no INPUT_FREE reason.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: With the origin/main versions of the two hooks: 2 failed, 12 passed. With this branch: 14 passed.

functions.name: _payload
functions.input: Hook payload JSON on stdin; TOOL_INPUT env as fallback
functions.output: The tool_input dict holding the Bash command the hook inspects
functions.if_none: Empty or invalid input gives {} and the hook allows

break_it.scenario: A future hook added to settings.json reads its input from the wrong place.
break_it.what_happens: It silently allows everything, as these three did for weeks.
break_it.how: test_every_registered_hook_has_a_case fails unless the hook has a must-react case or a named INPUT_FREE reason; test_hook_reacts_to_stdin_payload then sends the case on stdin.

break_it.scenario: A woken hook starts blocking ordinary commands.
break_it.what_happens: Every Bash call would be refused by the hook.
break_it.how: test_bash_hook_allows_a_harmless_command sends `git status` to every Bash hook; replay of 30 real commands blocked 0.

break_it.scenario: no-unreferenced-new-file runs before the whole command, so `git add new.py && git commit` stages the file after the hook looked.
break_it.what_happens: That new file is not checked.
break_it.how: Known limit of a PreToolUse hook; recorded here, not fixed in this PR.
break_it.repro: Send `git add x.py && git commit -m y` with x.py unstaged: exit 0.

post_merge.manual_verify: Restart Claude Code so the hook list reloads.
